infrastructure: Bosnia has improving urban broadband, with EU-supported infrastructure investment.
Complex political structure (two entities) slows coordinated infrastructure deployment.
Mobile connectivity is widespread, partially compensating for fixed broadband gaps.
talent: University of Sarajevo has computer science programmes with emerging tech talent.
A growing IT outsourcing sector provides applied development experience.
Brain drain to EU countries (particularly Germany and Austria) is severe.
governance: Bosnia's complex Dayton Agreement governance structure severely hampers coordinated national policy, including AI strategy.
GDPR-aligned data protection law is in place; Personal Data Protection Agency is the regulator.
Slow EU accession progress reflects deep governance challenges.
investment: EU pre-accession IPA funds support digital transformation.
Very limited AI-specific foreign investment due to governance complexity.
IT outsourcing sector is attracting some international clients.
economic_readiness: Constrained economic development due to political fragmentation and governance challenges.
IT sector is growing as a source of employment and foreign exchange.
Low GDP per capita limits domestic AI adoption.
